sources.fullCitation: Deutsche Nationalbibliothek. “Ninon.” Jan Kiepura, tenor, with orchestra. Odeon O-4661; coupled with “Oh Madonna!”. Linked catalogue record 380669366, identified by the coupling reference in record 380669358. Supplementary recording data: Gesellschaft für Historische Tonträger, Odeon matrix discography, Be 10000 series, entry Be 10221, Berlin, 7 February 1933; conductor Frieder Weissmann.
sources.title: Ninon, lach mir einmal zu — Odeon O-4661, catalogue and matrix evidence
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura
sources.researchNote: DNB record 380669358 describes the coupled “Oh Madonna!” side, with Be.10220-2 and WBe.10220-2 as matrix forms; its field 777 explicitly links “Ninon” as record 380669366. The primary URL follows that link, not a guessed identifier. The separate GHT matrix discography identifies “Ninon” as Be 10221, recorded in Berlin on 7 February 1933 with Jan Kiepura and Frieder Weissmann. The structured date describes that session, not a DNB issue date. Neither the coupled side’s take suffix nor the matrix is transferred to “Ninon”. The corrected catalogue identifier is established by DNB’s coupling metadata; direct retrieval of the linked record was rate-limited during this review, and the full GHT PDF was unavailable for download.

contributions.scopeNote: DNB’s coupled-side record explicitly links “Ninon” as record 380669366. The independent GHT matrix entry Be 10221 names Jan Kiepura, tenor, with orchestra directed by Frieder Weissmann. The coupled “Oh Madonna!” matrix Be.10220-2 is not evidence for a take of “Ninon”.
